comment:
Thank you for the synthetic stream. It gives reliable steps to reproduce.

**Analysis**

This analysis comes from the code and the attached segments. Nobody ran a build yet. Two problems combine.

1. A false discontinuity in MSE. The demuxer clamps the first AAC sample (pts -1008/48000) to time 0, and its duration becomes 16/48000. In [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2286), this short duration becomes `mLongestFrameDuration`. The next audio frame is 1024/48000 later, more than two times that value. The check at [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2124) then reports "Discontinuity detected" and calls `ResetAppendState()` on all tracks. Thus the video track needs a new random access point.
2. No random access point in video `seg1.mp4` on macOS. Since bug 2049615, the macOS demuxer accepts only HEVC IDR frames as keyframes, not CRA frames ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#477)). The x265 encoder uses open GOP, so `seg1.mp4` has only CRA frames. MSE drops all video frames of `seg1.mp4`, and `buffered` stays at the video end of `seg0.mp4`.

This also explains your table. The x264 encoder writes an IDR at each keyframe, so H.264 recovers at `seg1.mp4`. The control stream has a positive audio tfdt, so no sample is clamped. This is a gap in the fix for bug 2026875, not a regression of it. Windows and Linux probably do not show the stall, because the CRA rule applies only on macOS. Nobody checked this yet.

**Fix direction**

Do not let a sample that the demuxer trimmed set the frame duration limit in `ProcessFrames`. Use the original sample duration, or the decode time step, instead. A second option is to accept a CRA frame with the container sync flag as a random access point in MSE. The attached stream can become a mochitest that checks that `buffered` grows past the first segment.
title: HLS fMP4 with HEVC video stalls at the end of the first segment when the audio track's decode time starts negative (tfdt stored as 2^64−N)

This looks like an AMD driver crash in the hardware H.264 encoder MFT. Firefox reaches it only on Nightly, through the GPU process encoder.

**Analysis**

- All four signatures crash on the `MediaPEncoder #1` thread in the GPU process. All reports are from Nightly 154 to 160, on AMD GPUs (vendor 0x1002).
- Each report has the same fault: a read of address 0x40 at `amdh264enc64.dll+0x35fcb`. This is a null pointer inside the driver.
- The stack of [crash 3c084ef6](https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/3c084ef6-fa60-48ac-96b3-c90290261002) goes through `WMFMediaDataEncoder::ProcessDrain`, `MFTEncoder::Drain` and `MFTEncoder::DrainAsync` ([MFTEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFTEncoder.cpp#1115)). The drain path follows the async MFT event protocol, so the bad read is in the driver.
- Most reports are on device 0x1638 with driver 31.0.21923.11000 on Windows 11. The `MFTEventSource::GetEvent` reports are on device 0x67df with driver 31.0.21924.61 on Windows 10.
- In two dual GPU reports, the loaded `amdh264enc64.dll` version matches the driver of the second AMD GPU. `MFTEncoder::EnumEncoders` does not select an adapter.
- The crashes occur 2 to 3 seconds after the GPU process starts. A likely caller is the encode check of the gfx sanity test from bug 2067454 ([SanityTestChecks.sys.mjs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/toolkit/components/gfx/SanityTestChecks.sys.mjs#229)). That test runs again after each Nightly update.

**Regression**

Only Nightly enables `media.use-remote-encoder.video.platform` and `media.gpu-process-encoder` ([StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#12667)). Bug 2044973 enabled them, so it is set as the regressor, as on bug 2048390.

**Fix direction**

The AMD encoder blocklist entry from bug 2048390 ([GfxInfo.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/windows/GfxInfo.cpp#1528)) blocks only drivers older than 31.0.0.0. All crashing drivers are 31.x or 32.x, so that entry does not apply. Suggest a new `FEATURE_HARDWARE_VIDEO_ENCODING` entry for these drivers or for the affected GCN device family. As an option, select the encoder for the compositor adapter with `MFTEnum2` and its adapter LUID attribute.

Suggest that aosmond, who fixed bug 2048390, takes this bug.
title: Crash in [@ amdh264enc64.dll | RtlpWaitOnCriticalSection] on GCN Radeon graphics

Thank you for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

The silence comes from how the audio sink handles a failed open on the default output device. Firefox does not try again when a device appears later.

1. With no output device, the audio stream does not open. [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#654) then tries again later only for a device set with `setSinkId()`. For the default device, it rejects the "ended" promise ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#676)).
2. [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4675) then marks the audio as complete. Because the media has video, playback continues without audio.
3. After this, `NeedAudioSink()` always returns false ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#461)). Thus the periodic retry, the resume path and unmute never open a new stream.

Pause and resume only change the playing state, so the failed state stays. A seek stops and starts the media sink. This makes a new "ended" promise and opens a new stream on the new device. A reload or a new tab also makes a new sink.

**Fix direction**

When the default device fails and the media has video, suggest that `AudioSinkWrapper` keeps the "ended" promise pending and calls `ScheduleRetrySink()`. The `setSinkId()` path from bug 1829054 already does this. Audio-only media can keep the current error. As an option, the retry can start on `CubebDeviceEnumerator::OnAudioOutputDeviceListChange()` ([CubebDeviceEnumerator.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/webrtc/CubebDeviceEnumerator.h#51)) instead of on a timer.

This bug does not look like a regression. Bug 1636722 fixed a different case, where no tab had audio after a device connected. This bug now blocks bug 2011679, the meta bug for Bluetooth device audio and video.

No more data is necessary from you at this time.
title: Playing tab stays silent after Bluetooth connects

**Analysis**

The crash data agrees with the cause in comment 0. In [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4744), `RequestDebugInfo` returns a pending promise when `OwnerThread()->Dispatch` fails. The function checks the result only with a `MOZ_ASSERT`. When the dispatch fails, the runnable releases its reference to the promise immediately. Then the lambda in [MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1660) drops the last reference to that pending promise. The `FirstFrameLoaded` ThenValue from [MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844) stays on a chained promise, and `AssertIsDead` crashes.

`MediaFormatReader::RequestDebugInfo` in [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3437) has the same problem. It uses `InvokeAsync`, which ignores the dispatch result. The main thread hop in `MediaDecoder::RequestDebugInfo` has the same exposure. The data does not show why the task queue stops before `mShuttingDown` becomes true.

The check that crashes is enabled only in debug, Nightly and Developer Edition builds. On Release, the only effect is one lost `first_frame_loaded` telemetry sample. In the last 30 days, 22 crash reports show this crash reason. The closed intermittent bugs 1896281 and 1899996 show the same failure in CI.

This problem started with bug 1888265. That change added the `FirstFrameLoaded` call. It also changed the dispatch check from `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT` to `MOZ_ASSERT`.

**Next steps**

The recommended fix is to reject the promise when the dispatch fails in `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo`. The same change also applies to `MediaFormatReader::RequestDebugInfo` and to the main thread hop. `FirstFrameLoaded` already handles a rejection. The open needinfo on :[person] covers the next step.

This is a confirmed defect in the `VideoFrame` constructor for an `ImageBitmap` source. The attached testcase gives reliable steps to reproduce.

**Analysis**

`ImageBitmap::ToCloneData()` returns the source surface without premultiplication, and it puts the alpha type in `mAlphaType`. The `VideoFrame` constructor wraps only the surface and ignores `mAlphaType`, as the TODO in [VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1749) shows. At draw time, `nsLayoutUtils::SurfaceFromVideoFrame` reports `gfxAlphaType::Premult` for all formats with alpha. Thus the draw path reads unpremultiplied bytes as premultiplied bytes. A direct draw of the `ImageBitmap` is correct, because `ImageBitmap::PrepareForDrawTarget` premultiplies a `NonPremult` surface. This gap exists since bug 1774300 added the constructor, so it is not a regression.

**Fix direction**

In the constructor, premultiply a `NonPremult` surface with alpha into a new `DataSourceSurface`, as `PrepareForDrawTarget` does. The same copy can crop to `mPictureRect`, which is the problem in bug 1939711. The open revision [D330607](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D330607) on bug 1939711 now has the title "Handle ImageBitmap source's crop and alpha type". We recommend that its review confirm that it premultiplies `NonPremult` surfaces. If it does, this bug can close as a duplicate of bug 1939711 when that patch lands.

The patch on bug 2079836 changes only the RGBA and BGRA buffer path. If both patches land, make sure that no path premultiplies the pixels two times.

This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.
title: VideoFrame created from an unpremultiplied ImageBitmap is drawn with wrong colors

comment:
Thank you for the report and the xscreensaver log.

**Analysis**

This is a regression in Firefox 146, in the GTK wake lock code. Bug 1665986 made the GTK listener act on the `audio-playing` wake lock, in [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1121). Then bug 1996504 changed the background test in [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1126). Since that change, an audio lock in a foreground tab uses the idle inhibit. Thus the screensaver does not start while audible media plays.

On other platforms, the audio wake lock only prevents system sleep. Windows uses `PowerRequestExecutionRequired` in [nsAppShell.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/windows/nsAppShell.cpp#81). macOS uses `kIOPMAssertionTypeNoIdleSleep` in [nsAppShell.mm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/cocoa/nsAppShell.mm#82). Before this, bug 1749187 removed `audio-playing` from the GTK listener on purpose, so that audio playback did not stop the screensaver.

No pref turns off the audio wake lock. The `media.video-wakelock` pref controls only the video wake lock. [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#5442) takes the audio wake lock for all audible playback.

Suggested fix direction: in the GTK `WakeLockListener::Callback`, always treat `audio-playing` as a suspend-only lock. Then audio never uses the idle inhibit, as on Windows and macOS. Background audio still prevents system sleep.

This bug is related to bug 1885268, which is about the video wake lock. This bug blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980.

**Next steps**

The code at fault is in `widget/gtk`, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk. Martin, could you please look at this bug? You wrote the changes in bug 1665986 and bug 1996504.
title: Firefox unconditionally inhibits the screensaver even when only audio is playing

Thank you for the detailed analysis and the `chrt` test.

**Analysis**

The code confirms the cause. On Linux, `GraphRunner` never gets real-time priority. In [GraphRunner.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/GraphRunner.cpp#121), `#ifndef XP_LINUX` removes the promotion, and the demotion at line 150 has the same guard. The only boost left is `PRIORITY_HIGHEST` at [GraphRunner.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/GraphRunner.cpp#48), and your `ps` output shows that the thread stays at nice 0.

In single-thread mode, `GraphRunner::OneIteration()` runs on the real-time audio callback thread. It waits in `mMonitor.Wait()` until `GraphRunner` completes the iteration ([GraphRunner.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/GraphRunner.cpp#88)). Thus a short CPU burst delays the real-time thread too. Single-thread mode is on by default in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#3576).

Bug 1653667 added the guard in 2020 to fix a `SIGXCPU` crash. Thus this bug is a regression from that change. Bug 1605033 promoted the thread, but that fix does not apply on Linux.

**Fix direction**

Removing the guard is not sufficient. Content processes set `RLIMIT_RTTIME` and use one flag for the full process in [UnderrunHandlerLinux.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/UnderrunHandlerLinux.cpp#17). Graph code reads that flag only at the start of an iteration. A long AudioWorklet in one iteration can thus hit the hard limit, and the kernel then stops the process.

1. Make demotion safe first, as bug 1628198 describes. For example, a watchdog thread can demote the thread by its thread id.
2. Promote `GraphRunner` through the parent process, as the AudioIPC client callback thread does with `PromoteThreadToRealTime` in [context.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/audioipc2-client/src/context.rs#73).
3. Gecko C++ cannot use that path at this time. It needs a new audioipc2 export or a new Gecko IPC message.

A smaller first step can be to promote `GraphRunner` only when the graph has no AudioWorklet. This bug now blocks bug 1951155, the meta bug for audio crackling.
title: GraphRunner is not real-time on Linux, so WebRTC playback glitches under transient load

Thank you for the detailed report, the logs and the tested patch.

**Analysis**

The attached logs confirm the cause. In the 8-bit H.264 log, plane 0 (R8) imports with zero copy. Plane 1 (GR88) fails with `EGL_BAD_MATCH`, and the decoder then starts again in software. In the 10-bit log, plane 1 (GR1616) imports with zero copy on every frame. The driver format list has R8, R16, GR1616 and NV12, but no GR88 and no RG88.

On the VA-API path, the plane formats come from the driver export descriptor in [DMABufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp#1641). Bug 2021722 and bug 2052037 added a GR88 to RG88 swap in `DMABufSurfaceYUV::CreateTexture()` ([DMABufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp#2099)). The swap needs RG88 modifiers, so it does nothing on this driver. When `eglCreateImage` fails, the function returns false at [DMABufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp#2165). The copy fallback `CreateTextureViaCopyYUV()` ([DMABufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp#2246)) needs an EGL image, so it never runs.

**Fix direction**

The approach in patch v2 (attachment 9656430) is correct. After the two-channel import fails, it imports plane 1 as `DRM_FORMAT_R16` and copies it into the RG8 texture. R16 and RG8 have the same 16-bit texel size, so the copy keeps the bytes. Before it lands, we suggest these changes:

1. Rebase the patch on the current mozilla-central.
2. Use the R16 path only for `DRM_FORMAT_MOD_LINEAR` planes, as the existing copy fallbacks do.
3. Keep the R16 choice for the surface format, so that `eglCreateImage` does not fail on every frame.
4. Find the fourcc attribute by its name, not by the index `attribs[5]`.

A single NV12 EGL image would remove the copy, but Firefox has no such import path, and it needs new WebRender work. Note: on this driver, the reporter uses local shims to run WebRender on the GPU.

This bug blocks bug 1610199 (Linux VA-API playback) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

**Next steps**

Martin, could you please look at this analysis and at the reporter's patch?
title: VA-API: 8-bit NV12 video falls back to software on Arm Mali (libmali): DMABufSurfaceYUV imports plane 1 as GR88, the driver offers neither GR88 nor RG88 (EGL_BAD_MATCH) although it offers whole-frame NV12

comment:
Thank you for the test page and the clear steps.

**Analysis**

The attached WebM has VP9 video with a keyframe every 2 seconds. It has Opus audio with an 80 ms SeekPreRoll. The Cues list only the video track.

1. `fastSeek(7.9)` puts the video on the 6.0 s keyframe. Then the audio seeks to 6.0 s.
2. For Opus, [WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1172) subtracts the 80 ms pre-roll from the target. The last cue at or before 5.92 s is at 4.0 s, so the audio starts near 4.0 s.
3. Vorbis and MP4 have no pre-roll, so their audio starts at 6.0 s.
4. A fast seek does not trim the audio. The fast branch in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1821) keeps the first audio sample, and the clock starts at 6.0 s.
5. On seek resume, `AudioSinkWrapper` does not call `DropAudioPacketsIfNeeded`. This is true for the async start path ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#596)) and for the stream reuse path ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#616)).

Thus audio from about 4.0 s plays against a 6.0 s clock. The sound is about 2 seconds behind the picture.

The seek resume code used to drop this early audio. Bug 2055541 (Part 1) removed the drop from the async start path. Bug 2052692 (Part 3) added the stream reuse path without a drop. This result comes from reading the code, not from a bisection.

**Fix direction**

On seek resume, call `DropAudioPacketsIfNeeded` with the seek start time on both paths. Another option is to drop the audio that ends before the video seek time in the fast seek branch of `MediaDecoderStateMachine`.

Thank you for the public test page and the profile.

**Analysis**

The profile in comment 1 shows the problem clearly. Audio decodes 2 to 3.5 seconds ahead of video. The video track waits for network data, but playback does not stop to buffer.

1. The state machine does not see that video is starved. For a progressive download, the demuxer read blocks in the media cache. Thus `IsWaitingVideoData()` stays false, and the `OutOfDecodedVideo` buffering check never starts ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3195)).
2. The buffering heuristic uses the later decoded end of audio and video ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4238)). Audio is ahead, so the heuristic does not count the gap behind video. In the profile, each buffering period ends after 40 to 120 ms.
3. The audio clock continues past the decoded video. Then `MediaFormatReader::ShouldSkip` finds the next keyframe behind the media time and skips to it ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#1464)). The MP4 index gives the keyframe time before its data arrives. In the profile, video jumps from 2.4 s to 8.0 s, and from 10.5 s to 16.0 s.

The second video on the page has no audio track. Thus no clock runs ahead of the video, and no skip occurs.

**Fix direction**

- Make `HasLowBufferedData` start from the earliest decoded end of the tracks that still decode.
- Stay in buffering while video has no decoded frames and its data at the media time is not buffered.
- In `ShouldSkip`, do not skip when the buffered video data does not reach the target keyframe.

The test page reproduces the problem every time. This bug now blocks bug 1416090, the meta bug for dropped video frames.

**Analysis**

Gecko does not follow the spec here. whatwg/html PR 13043 is merged. The [resource selection algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#concept-media-load-algorithm) now sets *candidate* to null when the candidate is removed or moved out. The "failed with elements" step then fires no `error` event.

Root cause: the media element keeps the current `<source>` in `mSourceLoadCandidate`, set in `GetNextSource` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#7665)). `ContentWillBeRemoved` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2373)) moves only `mSourcePointer` back. It does not change `mSourceLoadCandidate`.

On a failure, `NotifyLoadError` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#3041)) and `DecodeError` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#6421)) call `DispatchAsyncSourceError(mSourceLoadCandidate, ...)`. `nsSourceErrorEventRunner::Run` ([MediaElementEventRunners.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/utils/MediaElementEventRunners.cpp#170)) checks only the load id. A child removal does not change the load id, so the event fires at the detached `<source>`.

**Fix direction**

In `ContentWillBeRemoved`, mark the candidate as removed when `aChild` is `mSourceLoadCandidate`. A move also goes through this path. In `NotifyLoadError` and `DecodeError`, skip the `error` event for a removed candidate, but still call `QueueLoadFromSourceTask()`. Do not only set `mSourceLoadCandidate` to null: the null branch does not go to the next source, so resource selection stops.

**Tests**

WPT PR 63347 is not synced yet. These in-tree tests still expect `error` at the removed or moved source, and need an update with the fix:

- [resource-selection-candidate-remove-onerror.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/testing/web-platform/tests/html/semantics/embedded-content/media-elements/loading-the-media-resource/resource-selection-candidate-remove-onerror.html)
- [resource-selection-candidate-remove-addEventListener.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/testing/web-platform/tests/html/semantics/embedded-content/media-elements/loading-the-media-resource/resource-selection-candidate-remove-addEventListener.html)

No team meta bug applies to this bug.

Thank you for the detailed audit and the PoC files.

**Analysis**

The race in this report cannot occur. With frame threading, libavcodec calls `get_buffer2` only through `thread_get_buffer_internal()`. That function holds `buffer_mutex` around the call. All frame threads of one codec context share this mutex. Thus `GetVideoBufferWrapper()` never runs on two threads at the same time.

The check and the `Some(true)` store in `GetVideoBuffer()` run under that lock. The `Some(false)` store in `GetVideoBufferDefault()` also runs under it. After the flag becomes false, it stays false. Thus a default pool buffer never gets to the `ImageBufferWrapper` cast in the output path of [FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp).

The lock is in the vendored ffvpx, in [pthread_frame.c](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/media/ffvpx/libavcodec/pthread_frame.c). It is also in system FFmpeg from 4.0, in [pthread_frame.c on GitHub](https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/release/4.0/libavcodec/pthread_frame.c). The custom allocator needs libavutil 56 or later, which is FFmpeg 4.0. Also, the vendored ffvpx has no H.264 decoder. On Linux, H.264 uses the system FFmpeg library.

**Next steps**

We resolve this bug as INVALID, because the reported interleaving cannot occur. A developer can file a separate bug to harden the output path. For example, the decoder can check the buffer free callback before the cast.

**Analysis**

This crash is a Rust panic in the parent process on macOS, so the whole browser closes. Crash-stats shows 40 crashes in the last 6 months, mostly on arm64 with macOS 26. The crashes come from release, beta, nightly and ESR.

The assert that fires is `assert_ne!(id, kAudioObjectUnknown)` in `get_stream_virtual_format` ([device_property.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/device_property.rs#397)). `get_channel_count` gives each stream ID to that function ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#1747)). The caller `audiounit_get_devices_of_type` removes 0 device IDs first ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#2096)), so the 0 is a stream ID and not a device ID.

The 0 stream ID comes from `get_device_streams`. It makes a zero-filled vec from the first size query and fills it with a second query ([device_property.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/device_property.rs#257)). It does not truncate the vec to the size that the second query returns. When the stream list gets shorter between the two queries, 0 entries stay in the vec. The `ds.stream > id` filter removes them only for input devices ([device_property.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/device_property.rs#316)), so output devices crash.

In the crash report, a CoreAudio property-change notification runs on another thread at the same time. This agrees with a device list change between the two queries. The report cannot exclude a literal 0 from CoreAudio, but the fix below covers both cases.

**Regressor**

Bug 1670633 (the cubeb-coreaudio-rs update to 964e1462, November 2023) changed `get_channel_count` to call `get_device_streams` and `get_stream_virtual_format`. Before that change, this path had no stream ID assert. The signature first shows in build 20240118, which agrees with this change. Bug 1575883, which comment 0 names, is older than this call path. Bug 1902801 fixed a similar panic in `get_device_streams` for aggregate input devices only, so it does not cover this crash.

**Fix direction**

The fix belongs upstream in cubeb-coreaudio-rs, and then in a vendor update:

1. Truncate `streams` to the size that the second query returns in `get_device_streams`.
2. Remove `kAudioObjectUnknown` stream IDs for all device types, not only for input.
3. In `get_channel_count`, count a 0 stream ID as 0 channels instead of asserting.
4. Apply the same truncation in `get_devices` ([device_property.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/device_property.rs#73)).

Because this crash closes the whole browser, we suggest that a developer decides if the highest severity applies. The open needinfo on :[person] stays for the developer review.

Thanks for the detailed report and the three profiles.

**Analysis**

All three profiles (153.4.0esr, 158.0 and 160.0a1) show the same hot path on the `CanvasRenderer` thread. Each `texImage2D(VideoFrame)` call does three full CPU passes over the 4K frame. Together they use about 70% of the thread, so one upload takes longer than one 16 ms frame.

1. `DataSourceSurfaceFromYCbCrDescriptor` allocates a `B8G8R8X8` surface ([ImageDataSerializer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/gfx/layers/ImageDataSerializer.cpp#357)). `Factory::CreateDataSourceSurface` always fills a `B8G8R8X8` surface with 0xFF ([Factory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/gfx/2d/Factory.cpp#781)). This `memset` uses about 31% of the thread.
2. The YUV to RGB conversion then writes every pixel again (`I422ToARGBRow_AVX2`, about 6%).
3. `TexUnpackBlob::ConvertIfNeeded` converts `BGRX8` to `RGBA8` into a new `calloc` buffer ([TexUnpackBlob.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/canvas/TexUnpackBlob.cpp#488)). The `WebGLTexelConversions::pack<20>` step uses about 33% to 35% of the thread.

On the content main thread, `createImageBitmap(frame)` waits on a synchronous `RemoteMediaManagerChild::Readback`. This wait matches the 9 to 14 ms cost that you measured. The same path is in ESR 153, so this is not a recent regression.

**Fix direction**

- Do not clear the surface when the YUV conversion writes every pixel.
- Convert the YUV data directly into the format that the upload needs. Then `ConvertIfNeeded` has no work to do. This matches the texture format idea in comment 4.
- As a longer-term option, upload the Y, Cb and Cr planes and convert them in a shader.

The code at fault is in `gfx/2d`, `gfx/layers` and `dom/canvas`. Graphics owns this code, and `TexUnpackBlob.cpp` maps to Core :: Graphics: CanvasWebGL. The bug stays in this component because the try push in comment 4 already works on a fix. A person can move it to Graphics: CanvasWebGL if that team takes the patch.

This bug now blocks bug 1676924 (4K and above frame drops). Your offer in comment 5 to test the try build on your Linux machine is useful, because the developer's Linux machine is not available now.

Thank you for the bisection and the sample file.

**Analysis**

The pushlog has two changes. Only bug 2066858 is a media change. It sets `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` to true on Nightly for all platforms. Before that change, the pref was true only on macOS. The stream reuse code came from bug 2052692. Bug 2066858 only exposed the problem on Linux.

The likely cause is in the check that decides whether the audio stream can be reused. [AudioSink.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.h#90) `IsStreamDrained()` returns `mPlaybackComplete`. [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#817) sets this flag only when cubeb reports `CUBEB_STATE_DRAINED`.

At the end of the audio track, `AudioStream::DataCallback` gives cubeb fewer frames than it asks for. On PulseAudio, [stream.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/third_party/rust/cubeb-pulse/src/backend/stream.rs#1199) then stops the data callbacks. It reports DRAINED later, after a timer of about two output latencies. During this window, the stream is dead, but `IsStreamDrained()` still returns false.

A seek in this window keeps the old stream. [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/3934f7874da5d43c3eac71e6f44e0afe79d9071f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#710) `Stop()` stashes the sink, and `Start()` reuses it. `AudioStream::Resume` does not restart cubeb, because the stream is still marked as started. When the timer fires, DRAINED resolves the new ended promise. `OnAudioEnded` then shuts down the sink, and the video continues without audio. This agrees with your note that the problem occurs when the seek starts near the end.

**Fix direction**

Set a "drain started" flag in `AudioStream::DataCallback` before the short return. Clear the flag only when cubeb starts again. Make `IsStreamDrained()`, or a new `IsStreamDraining()`, return true in this state. Then `Stop()`, `Start()` and `ResumeStashedAudioSink()` create a new stream instead of the dead one.

This bug blocks the meta bug 2049891 (video decoding and seeking performance). It also affects the plan in bug 2059525 to enable the pref on more platforms. We suggest that the owner of bug 2052692 takes this bug.

**Next steps**

You do not need to do anything. As a workaround until a fix lands, set `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` to false in `about:config`.

The attached profile shows the cause of the start. YouTube calls `MediaCapabilities.decodingInfo()` for a 4K AV1 stream. The Data Decoder (RDD) process then creates a Vulkan decoder on the RTX 4060, and destroys it at once. No video decodes.

After the `VkDevice` is destroyed, no Gecko thread is busy. But the RDD process stays at about one full CPU core until the profile ends. Thus the busy thread is not a Gecko thread. It is most likely an NVIDIA driver thread that does not stop at device teardown.

The mozregression range has one changeset, from bug 2067742. On this path, the only new code that runs is the device creation in [hwcontext_vulkan.c](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/9046137a91a4614ad5be3448370a8265de01affc/media/ffvpx/libavutil/hwcontext_vulkan.c#1007). It also adds an NVIDIA optical flow queue in `setup_queue_families` ([hwcontext_vulkan.c](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/9046137a91a4614ad5be3448370a8265de01affc/media/ffvpx/libavutil/hwcontext_vulkan.c#1775)). comment:
Thanks for the review findings.

**Analysis**

The five findings are only in D278547 (bug 2005072). That patch is not in mozilla-central now, because the sheriffs backed it out on 2026-10-15. A code read of the [autoland push](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/commit/146655b7da2d) confirms all five findings in the patched [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/9046137a91a4614ad5be3448370a8265de01affc/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp). The check was a code read, not a test run.

Finding 1 changes the default behavior. The patch parses `loading` as an enum also when `media.lazy_loading.enabled` is off, which is the default in the patch. Thus `ChangeDelayLoadStatus()` sees the Lazy state and does not delay the document `load` event. This applies to every `<video>` or `<audio>` with `loading=lazy` and a source.

Findings 2 to 5 have one cause. The patch enters the lazy state from attribute changes, and it resumes through `DoLoad()`. `AbortExistingLoads()` then sees `NETWORK_IDLE`, fires `abort` and `emptied`, and restarts a load that is in progress. The early return in `DoLoad()` skips `SetPlaybackRate()`, `SetPlayedOrSeeked(false)` and `ResetState()`. `Load()` and `Play()` stop the observer, and nothing calls `nsVideoFrame::UpdatePosterSource()` after that.

**Fix direction**

We recommend one helper for the spec's "will lazy load element steps". It checks the pref, the Lazy state, `IsScriptEnabled()` and `!IsStaticDocument()`. All five findings are correct against [D278547](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D278547) (bug 2005072), with one correction to item 5. The patch is not in mozilla-central now. Its last landing was backed out on 2026-10-15.

**Analysis**

1. `ChangeDelayLoadStatus()` checks only the `loading` attribute. It does not check `media.lazy_loading.enabled`, `IsScriptEnabled()` or `IsStaticDocument()`. Thus with the pref off, `loading=lazy` stops the delay of the document `load` event.
2. A change of `loading` to `lazy` on an eager element calls `SetLazyLoading()`. When the element enters the viewport, `DoLoad()` loads the resource again from the start. While the element waits, the early return in `DoLoad()` ignores `src` changes.
3. Each resume path calls `DoLoad()`: the intersection observer, `play()` and the change to eager. Because `SetLazyLoading()` sets `NETWORK_IDLE`, `AbortExistingLoads()` queues `abort` and `emptied` before `loadstart`.
4. `load()` and `play()` call `StopLazyLoading(StartLoad::No)`, which stops the observation of the element. The patched `nsVideoFrame` does not load the poster while the element is lazy, so the poster does not appear.
5. On a `src` change of a lazy element, `DoLoad()` returns early. Correction: `SetPlaybackRate(mDefaultPlaybackRate)`, `SetPlayedOrSeeked(false)` and `ResetState()` run late, when the element enters the viewport. That later `DoLoad()` also fires a second `abort` and `emptied` pair.

**Fix direction**

- Add one helper for the spec's "will lazy load element steps": the pref, the Lazy state, `IsScriptEnabled()` and `!IsStaticDocument()`. Use it in `ChangeDelayLoadStatus()` to fix item 1.
- Enter the lazy state only from `SelectResource()`, and remove the early return in `DoLoad()`. `AfterSetAttr()` then handles only the change from lazy to eager. This fixes items 2 and 5.
- On resume, continue the held fetch. Do not call `DoLoad()`, and do not set `NETWORK_IDLE`. This fixes item 3.
- Keep the media resumption and the poster resumption separate. `load()` and `play()` clear only the media resumption, and the element stays observed for the poster. This fixes item 4.

The `loadstart` timing on resume waits on [whatwg/html issue 12973](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12973). Chrome and the current WPT tests delay `loadstart`, but the spec text does not.

We suggest that these fixes go into D278547 before the next landing. The code did not land, so this bug is not a regression. No media team meta bug applies to lazy loading.

This assertion is a regression from bug 2052692, which keeps the AudioSink for reuse across a seek. Bug 2052692 landed on 2026-07-14, the build that failed here contains it, and the first failure is on the same day.

**Analysis**

`AccurateSeekingState::DoSeek` stops the sink, then `ResetDecode()` empties the audio queue. With `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek`, a seek does not shut the sink down. The wrapper keeps it, and `PrepareForReuse` only marks the old audio in the ring buffer as stale.

If the state machine shuts the kept sink down during the seek, for example in `SuspendMediaSink` when the document goes inactive, `AudioSink::ShutDown` calls `ReenqueueUnplayedAudioDataIfNeeded`. That function does not check `mStoppedForSeek`. Thus it pushes the old pre-seek audio back into the empty queue. The first decoded sample after the seek then finds a queue that is not empty, and the assertion in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#2109) fails. See [AudioSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.cpp#211).

The failures were on macOS only until bug 2066858 turned the pref on in Nightly on all platforms. The failure count goes up each month. Bug 2065393 made the window smaller but did not close it. Bug 2067822 shows the same assertion on Android under the 1859384.mp4 tracking bug.

Release builds do not crash here. Because the pref is on in macOS release, a later resume of the sink can play some old audio again.

**Next steps**

The suggested fix is in `AudioSink::ShutDown`: when `mStoppedForSeek` is true, discard the ring buffer audio and do not put it back in the queue. Keep the state machine assertion. A gtest can cover this order. Keep the sink, and shut it down during the seek. Then give the first sample and check that the queue is empty.

Jim, this bug stays in the media team. Alastor Wu (alwu) wrote bug 2052692 and the related changes to this code.

Thank you for the patch stack. A check of the current tree confirms the five defects in comment 0. None of them is a regression: the code is old.

**Analysis**

- **Normalization and shared tables.** [PeriodicWave.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/webaudio/blink/PeriodicWave.cpp#157) limits the partials by the first frequency that asks for a table, and takes the normalization scale from that table. A lower frequency then rebuilds all tables in place. The built-in waves are shared per AudioContext through `BasicWaveFormCache`, so one oscillator can change the amplitude of another. The `(unsigned)(nyquist / fundamentalFrequency)` cast is also undefined for very small frequencies.
- **Phase on a waveform change.** [OscillatorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/webaudio/OscillatorNode.cpp#104) sets `mPhase` to 0 when the type changes to sine. After a change from sine to a table type, the engine reads the phase in radians as a table index.
- **Table selection.** In the render loop, [OscillatorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/webaudio/OscillatorNode.cpp#247) fetches the tables with the old `mFinalFrequency`. It updates the frequency for the current sample after that.
- **Extreme detune.** [OscillatorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/webaudio/OscillatorNode.cpp#167) does not clamp `frequency * mDetuneRatio` to the Nyquist limit. The float `mDetuneRatio` becomes infinite above about 153600 cents. The phase increment can then be infinite, or NaN at a frequency of 0. The two `detune-limiting.html` WPT subtests already fail.
- **Offline destination.** The offline destination track uses the generic external output path. [AudioNodeTrack.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/webaudio/AudioNodeTrack.cpp#501) appends each chunk to the track segment, but the destination engine already keeps a copy. The graph prunes the segment after about 50 ms, so this blocks buffer reuse but does not leak.

The approach in the patch stack matches these causes. Bug 1424902 reports the missing Nyquist clamp, so this stack can possibly fix it too. No team meta bug matches this area.

**Next steps**

The patch stack needs review from the Web Audio reviewers. The open needinfo for :[person] from BugBot stays as it is.

Thank you for the detailed analysis. The log excerpt and the code confirm it.

**Analysis**

The VA-API decoder is fast enough: the mean decode time stays below 1 ms per frame. The slow-decode check in [FFmpegDecodeStats.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegDecodeStats.cpp#50) counts each frame that takes longer than one frame duration. A frame that is 0.5 ms late counts the same as a frame that is 50 ms late.

The counter resets only after 3000 ms with no late frame ([FFmpegDecodeStats.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegDecodeStats.h#39)). With one late frame every 30 frames, it never resets. After 16 late frames, [FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp#1729) returns `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_DECODE_ERR` with "HW decoding is slow, switching back to SW decode".

Then `MediaFormatReader::Update()` shuts down the decoder and skips to the next keyframe, which causes the visible stall. If no later keyframe is buffered, it raises `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR` ("no_keyframe") in [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#2709). The attached excerpt shows this fatal error 9 µs after "Video needs a new decoder".

The new decoder is VA-API again, so the cycle repeats. One path is a reload of the player after the fatal error. Another path is a stream change, which sets `mHardwareDecodingDisabled = false` in [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#2205). Each new decoder starts again with zero late frames.

This logic has not changed since bug 1853024, so this is not a Firefox regression. More frequent clock changes on the AMD VCN probably make the late frames more frequent. Bug 2058347 hit the same check with Vulkan decoding, but its fix changed only the Vulkan code.

**Workarounds**

1. Set `media.ffmpeg.disable-software-fallback` to `true` in `about:config`.
2. Or set `media.av1.enabled` to `false` to make YouTube use another codec.

**Fix direction**

1. Decide that decoding is slow from sustained throughput, for example late frames in a sliding time window. Do not use a counter that needs 3 s with zero late frames.
2. Do not raise a fatal error when no keyframe is buffered. Keep the current decoder until the next keyframe.
3. Keep hardware decoding disabled for this stream when the check fires, also after a stream change.

Martin Stránský (stransky) wrote this check in bug 1750388. This bug blocks the Linux VA-API meta bug 1610199 and the Linux playback meta bug 1766429.

**Analysis**

The crash report is Fenix 160.0a1 Nightly on Android, on the `MediaSupervisor` thread. In the last 6 months, crash-stats shows 12 crashes with this signature. Ten are on Fenix 159 and 160 Nightly. Two are on desktop Firefox 153 beta and 157 release.

The cause looks like a race between a stale video seek and a new audio-only seek in `MediaFormatReader`:

1. [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#2856): `ResetDecode(aTracks)` rejects `mSeekPromise` and clears `mPendingSeekTime` for all tracks. It calls `ResetDemuxer()` only for the tracks in `aTracks`.
2. `ResetDemuxer()` disconnects `mSeekRequest` ([MediaFormatReader.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.h#599)). Thus `ResetDecode(audio)` leaves a running video demuxer seek alive.
3. A following `Seek(AudioOnly)` replaces `mOriginalSeekTarget` and starts an audio seek through `DoAudioSeek`.
4. When the old video seek resolves, `OnVideoSeekCompleted` sees a target that is not video-only ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3195)). It calls `DoAudioSeek` again, and the assert fails ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3274)).

The likely trigger is the seamless looping code in `MediaDecoderStateMachine`. `LoopingDecodingState::Exit` disconnects its seek requests but does not reset the reader ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#950)). A buffering transition or a change of `loop` can then create a new looping state. That state calls `ResetDecode(audio)` and `Seek(AudioOnly)` in `RequestDataFromStartPosition` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1096)) while the old video seek still runs. The crash stack does not show which state change occurred.

Clouseau says that `mPendingSeekTime` was set because the next line did not fault. That is not correct: the assert stops execution before the next line runs.

The regressor is not known. The code is from bug 1816852 and older bugs. The recent changes in bug 2078225 and bug 2076235 do not touch this seek state. Bug 1891129 is a fuzzer report of the same assert, closed as WONTFIX.

**Fix direction**

- In `ResetDecode`, also disconnect the `mSeekRequest` of the tracks that it does not reset. Or cancel the demuxer seek of the other track in `Seek()` or `AttemptSeek`.
- In `OnVideoSeekCompleted`, ignore a video seek result when the current target is `AudioOnly`.
- As a second step, `LoopingDecodingState::Exit` can call `ResetDecode` for each track whose seek request it disconnects.
- A gtest in `TestMediaFormatReader.cpp` can trigger the race every time. Start a video-only seek, call `ResetDecode(audio)` and `Seek(AudioOnly)`, then resolve the video seek.

No duplicate or media meta bug matches this crash.

Thanks for the sample file and the clear analysis. Comment 3 confirms the problem, and the upstream fix is in https://github.com/mozilla/mp4parse-rust/pull/459.

**Analysis**

The attached sample is a 15 second H.264 and Opus file, 1280x720 at 60 fps. For non-fragmented MP4, `read_edts` keeps the empty edit duration in the movie (`mvhd`) timescale ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/third_party/rust/mp4parse/src/lib.rs#4488)). Then `get_indice_table` uses this value without a conversion and subtracts `media_time`, which is in the track (`mdhd`) timescale ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/third_party/rust/mp4parse_capi/src/lib.rs#1579)). `create_sample_table` adds the result to each sample time in track ticks ([unstable.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/third_party/rust/mp4parse/src/unstable.rs#263)). For this file, the video start moves to 960 / 60 = 16 seconds, not 960 / 57600 = 16.7 ms.

Other code already converts this value correctly: `mp4parse_get_track_info` rescales it from the movie timescale to the track timescale ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/third_party/rust/mp4parse_capi/src/lib.rs#734)). The problem is not new: blame shows this code from the 2017 vendor update in bug 1343793.

Bug 2071559 reports the same defect with a different file. In that file, the video starts 833 ms late.

**Next steps**

The fix direction is to vendor mp4parse-rust PR 459 into `third_party/rust/mp4parse*` after it merges. The fix must rescale the empty edit duration in `get_indice_table`, as `mp4parse_get_track_info` does. This bug has the fix in progress, so we suggest that a triager closes bug 2071559 as a duplicate of this bug.

Thank you for the report. The overflow in this report cannot occur in the current code, so this is not a valid bug.

**Analysis**

`ReadUTF8()` in [BitReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/BitReader.cpp#118) rejects a first byte of `0xFE` or higher. Thus the frame number that [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#86) reads has a maximum of 31 bits. The largest block size is 65536 (`ReadBits(16) + 1`). The product in [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#109) is less than 2^47, and `int64_t` holds it with no overflow. The same limit applies to `ResetStartTimeIfNeeded()` in [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#326).

The arithmetic in the report is also not correct. `0xFFFFFFFFF * 65535` is `0xFFFEFFFFF0001`, a 52-bit value. Thus, even a 36-bit frame number does not overflow `uint64_t` or `int64_t`. The current code also uses `AssertedCast<int64_t>` on this result, not a plain assignment.

**Next steps**

This bug closes as INVALID. If a FLAC file causes a wrong index or a crash, please file a new bug and attach the file.

comment:
Thanks for the report.

**Analysis**

On Android and Windows, `MP4TrackDemuxer` does not check the NAL units of HEVC samples. The HEVC keyframe check in [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#476) is inside `#ifdef MOZ_APPLEMEDIA`. Bug 2049615 added it for macOS only. H.264 samples get the NAL check on all platforms, so only HEVC has this problem.

With no sync table and no sample flags, every sample has the container keyframe flag. `TrackBuffersManager` keeps that flag. A seek then starts decoding on a non-IRAP picture. The file has only one IDR, so the MediaCodec decoder and the MF decoder probably output no frame after the seek. The WMF MediaEngine path uses the same flag through `MFSampleExtension_CleanPoint` in [MFMediaEngineStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFMediaEngineStream.cpp#454), so it has the same cause.

`endOfStream()` only changes how the failure shows. Without it, `MediaFormatReader` waits for more data after the drain, and the seek stalls. With it, the seek completes at the end of the stream.

**Fix direction**

Run the existing HEVC check (`H265::IsKeyFrame` or `H265::IsRandomAccessPoint`) on all platforms in `MP4TrackDemuxer::GetNextSample()`. Keep the container flag when the sample does not parse. Use the same policy that bug 2072130 chooses for H.264. The "single-idr-no-stss" test in bug 2072130 can cover this change.

:[person], could you please confirm that MediaCodec can start decoding after a seek on a CRA picture? This decides if Android can use IRAP pictures as keyframes, or only IDR pictures.
title: Broken seeking in MSE on Android with H265 MP4 missing the stss box, only if endOfStream not called

The diagnosis in comment 0 is correct. The fix from this bug is on autoland now.

**Analysis**

With `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.direct-export.enabled`, `FFmpegVideoDecoder::ChooseVulkanPixelFormatFromContext` always adds `VK_IMAGE_USAGE_VIDEO_DECODE_DPB_BIT_KHR` to the decode image ([FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp#473)). The autoland change adds the bit only when FFmpeg already set it. Drivers that share one image for the DPB and the output, such as NVIDIA and Intel, still get the bit. The follow-up for older lavc versions in comment 8 is still open.

The RDNA3 report in comment 4 can have a different cause. A Nightly build with this fix will show if it does.

This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback). Bug 2077880 is a related direct-export problem on NVIDIA, with a different cause.

Thank you for the clear steps and the code analysis.

This is the same defect as bug 2083234. In that bug, a new load does not clear the start and end times of a media fragment URL (`#t=`). The old end time then triggers the fragment-end pause, and that pause uses a decoder that no longer exists. Your `load()` steps are one more trigger for the same cause. Thus we close this bug as a duplicate of bug 2083234.

**Analysis**

The current code matches your report. The fragment branch in `FireTimeUpdate` calls `mDecoder->SetFragmentEndTime()` with no null check ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#7804)). `AbortExistingLoads` shuts down the decoder, but it does not reset `mFragmentStart` or `mFragmentEnd` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2616)). With no decoder, `CurrentTime()` returns `mDefaultPlaybackStartPosition`, so the fragment condition stays true.

**Notes for the fix in bug 2083234**

- Reset `mFragmentStart` and `mFragmentEnd` on the load path, for example in `AbortExistingLoads`.
- Also add a null check before the `SetFragmentEndTime()` call. The inner `Pause()` in the same branch calls `DoLoad()` when the network state is `NETWORK_EMPTY`, and that can shut down the decoder.
- Use the steps in comment 0 as a crashtest for the `load()` trigger.

The crash ids in comment 0 are not complete, so we could not read the Windows and Android crash reports.

Thank you for the report. The multiplication in this report cannot overflow. The proof follows.

**Proof**

1. The code in comment 0 is not in the tree. `dom/media/flac/` has no `SetIndex()` and no `aPreviousBlocksize`. The real code computes `mIndex` in [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#109). It multiplies only for a fixed blocksize stream. A variable blocksize stream uses the coded number directly.
2. The coded number has at most 31 bits. [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#86) reads it with `BitReader::ReadUTF8()`. That function returns -1 for a first byte of `0xFE` or higher ([BitReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/BitReader.cpp#118)), and the caller then rejects the frame ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#87)). Thus the longest accepted number has 6 bytes, which is 31 bits.
3. The blocksize is at most 65536. The largest value is `ReadBits(16) + 1` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#100)).
4. Thus the product is at most (2^31 - 1) * 65536 = `0x7FFFFFFF0000`. This value has 47 bits. It fits in `uint64_t` and in `int64_t`, so no overflow and no undefined conversion occur. The same limits apply to the product in `ResetStartTimeIfNeeded()` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#326)).
5. The proof does not depend on `AssertedCast`. That cast checks only in debug builds. The value fits in all builds.
6. The numbers in the report also do not overflow. `0xFFFFFFFFF * 65535` is `0xFFFEFFFFF0001`, a 52-bit value, not `0xFFFEF0001FFFC0001`.
7. The impact in the report cannot follow. `mIndex` is a sample index. It sets only the frame time, in `Frame::Time()` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#337)). It is not a byte offset. The demuxer finds each frame in the file by a byte scan for the frame sync code. `TimeUnit` stores its ticks in a `CheckedInt64` ([TimeUnits.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/TimeUnits.h#266)), so the time conversion is also checked.

**Next steps**

The resolution is INVALID. If a FLAC file causes a crash, a sanitizer error or a wrong seek position in Firefox, please file a new bug and attach the file.

- **Root cause.** `ProcessMediaFragmentURI()` sets `mFragmentEnd` from the `#t=` fragment ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#6380)). `load()` calls `AbortExistingLoads()`, and `ShutdownDecoder()` sets `mDecoder` to null ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2605)). `AbortExistingLoads()` does not reset `mFragmentStart` or `mFragmentEnd` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2615)).
- **The crash.** With no decoder, `CurrentTime()` returns the stored start position, so the fragment check in `FireTimeUpdate()` is true. The branch then calls `mDecoder->SetFragmentEndTime()` with no null check ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#7917)).
- **Two paths.** A script `pause()` reaches `PauseInternal()` and then `FireTimeUpdate()` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#3888)). The stable-state task from `UnbindFromTree()` also calls `PauseInternal()`.
- **Crash Stats.** The signature `mozilla::dom::HTMLMediaElement::FireTimeUpdate` has 45 content-process crashes since April 2026, on Windows, Android, macOS and Linux. The two reports you name are bp-2a02d882-3e32-4598-a46d-175120260928 (Windows, from `pause()`) and bp-7c97682b-bfcf-43f3-974b-e781e0260930 (Android, from `UnbindFromTree()`). Both read address 0x0.
- **Related bug.** Bug 2083234 tracks the wider problem: the media element keeps stale state after a new source is loaded. This bug stays open because it tracks this crash signature.
- **Not a regression.** The call comes from the media fragment work in bug 648595, and the code is old.

This is a content-process crash: one tab crashes, and a reload recovers it. The volume is low, so the severity is S3.

**Next steps**

The fix is small and stays in `HTMLMediaElement.cpp`:

1. Reset `mFragmentStart` and `mFragmentEnd` in `AbortExistingLoads()`, before its own `FireTimeUpdate()` call.
2. Reset both fields at the start of `ProcessMediaFragmentURI()` in all cases. Now an old end time can go to the next decoder when the new source has no `#t=`.
3. Add an `mDecoder` null check before `SetFragmentEndTime()` in `FireTimeUpdate()`. Other `ShutdownDecoder()` callers also leave the fragment fields set.

The page in comment 0 can become a crashtest. A second version with `v.remove()` can cover the `UnbindFromTree()` path. No meta bug matches this crash.

**Analysis**

The about:support shows the Intel Arc (BMG G31) as the active GPU, and `HARDWARE_VIDEO_DECODING_VULKAN` is available. No modified pref explains the failure.

The Vulkan decoder selects its GPU in `SelectVulkanDecoderPhysicalDevice` in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#1067). The code uses the match with the renderer GPU only to sort the list. When no GPU matches, it takes the first discrete GPU. Comment 3 shows this result: the log says `matches renderer: false`, and the NVIDIA GPU wakes up on an Optimus laptop.

The NVIDIA check from bug 2067923 is `NvidiaDrmModesetDisabled` in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#913). It reads `/sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset`. When `nvidia-drm` is not loaded, this file does not exist, so the NVIDIA GPU stays a candidate. A GPU with no DRM node cannot export the decoded frame, so playback stops with "Failed to export NV12 FD". The fix for bug 2067923 is not in 155.0.1, and it does not cover a module that is not loaded.

Suggested fix direction:
1. When the renderer GPU is known and no Vulkan GPU matches it, do not use Vulkan decoding. Fall back to VA-API or software decoding on the renderer GPU.
2. Skip a GPU that has no DRM node. Treat a missing `nvidia_drm` module as unusable.

The pref `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.enabled` set to `false` in `about:config` turns off Vulkan decoding.

This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

Thank you for the profile in comment 2.

**Analysis**

The profile shows the cause. VA-API decoding in the RDD process works without errors. The stall is in the `MediaDecoderStateMachine` buffering logic, not in the decoder.

1. When the clip plays again after it ends, the state machine treats the seek to 0 as a warm seek ("startSinkAfterWarmSeek=true"). The code sets this flag in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3254).
2. With hardware decoding, a warm seek prerolls only 1 video frame. The pref `media.seek-resume.video-preroll-frames-hw` is 1 in [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#14132). Software decoding prerolls 3 frames, so it does not stall.
3. 1 frame is less than `LOW_VIDEO_FRAMES` (2), so `HasLowDecodedVideo()` is true immediately. The state machine enters buffering 2 ms after playback starts, through the check in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3204).
4. Buffering cannot end early for this file. The buffered range ends at 4.97 s (the end of the video track), but the duration is 5.0 s (the audio track). Thus `HasLowBufferedData()` stays true, and only the 15 s buffering timeout ends the wait ("Buffered for 15.271s").

This is a regression from bug 2050845, which added the warm seek preroll in Firefox 154. :[person] wrote that change.

**Fix direction**

- Keep the hardware warm preroll at or above `LOW_VIDEO_FRAMES`, or skip the low-data check until the queues refill after a warm resume.
- Do not treat a seek from the ended state as a warm seek.
- As a separate change, limit the `HasLowBufferedData()` end to the buffered end when the download is complete.

This bug blocks bug 1610199 (Linux VA-API playback) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback). Bug 2045880 shows a similar replay stall without hardware decoding, so it stays a related bug. :[person], the cause is now known, so a VA-API test of the sample is no longer necessary.

comment:
Thank you for the profile and the pref test.

**Analysis**

The profile shows the problem. Firefox creates the cubeb stream once and reuses it on each seek, as `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` allows. After a seek during playback, the audio clock includes the Bluetooth output latency of about 270 ms. After a seek while paused, the clock includes only about 30 ms. Thus the video runs about 250 ms ahead of the sound until the next seek.

The cause is in the reuse path for a paused stream:

1. A user pause stops the cubeb stream.
2. On the seek, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#725) keeps the stopped stream for reuse. This check does not test if cubeb still runs.
3. [AudioSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.cpp#362) restarts the stream with `Resume()`.
4. Because cubeb restarted, [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#533) rebases the clock with `CarryUnplayed::No`.

The macOS cubeb backend does not reset its frame count on stop. Thus the clock counts the frames that the stop dropped as played media. The clock then runs ahead of the sound by the output latency.

**Fix direction**

Two possible changes:

- In `AudioStream::RebaseLive`, carry the unplayed frames also when `Resume()` restarted cubeb.
- In `AudioSinkWrapper::Stop`, reuse only a stream whose cubeb still runs. A seek while paused then gets a new stream, as with the pref off.

A gtest for pause, seek and resume can cover the fix.

**Related bugs**

Bug 2052692 added the stream reuse. Bug 2071968 turned it on for macOS in the Firefox 158 release, which matches the start of the problem. Bug 2081761 reports audio dropouts with the same pref. Alastor Wu wrote this code. This bug now blocks the seek performance meta bug 2049891.

Until a fix lands, the workaround from comment 0 stays valid: set `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` to `false`.

Thank you for the detailed report and the patch.

**Analysis**

The cause in comment 0 is correct. The ffmpeg58 header set mixes the FFmpeg 4.4.1 `avcodec.h` from bug 1745284 with the FFmpeg 4.0 version files. [version.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavcodec/version.h#31) still says 58.18.100, and [version.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavutil/version.h#82) still says 56.14.100.

Thus `FF_API_OLD_ENCDEC`, `FF_API_THREAD_SAFE_CALLBACKS` and `FF_API_DEBUG_MV` remove three `AVCodecContext` fields that the real libavcodec 58 has. The first one, `refcounted_frames`, is in front of `qmin` in [avcodec.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavcodec/avcodec.h#1353). The values that [FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#504) writes to `qmin` and `qmax` go to the wrong fields. libx264 then opens with a minimum QP of 35.

The layout error starts with bug 1745284. It became visible when bug 1903582 made `FFmpegVideoEncoder` set `qmin` and `qmax`. Bug 1909369 later changed the values to the current prefs. Also, `FF_API_BUFFER_SIZE_T` is not defined, so `AVPacketSideData.size` has the wrong type. Firefox does not read that field today.

**Fix direction**

Replace both ffmpeg58 version files with the FFmpeg 4.4.1 copies, as D333609 does. All libavcodec 58 releases use the same layout, so this is also correct for FFmpeg 4.0 to 4.3. A `static_assert` on `offsetof(AVCodecContext, qmin)` for each header set can catch a partial update in the future. The reviewer should know that `FFmpegVideoDecoder` now also sets `thread_safe_callbacks = 1` with libavcodec 58.

This bug is now linked to the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.
title: WebCodecs H.264 encoder ignores bitrate with system FFmpeg 4.x: stale ffmpeg58 version.h shifts AVCodecContext, x264 opens with qmin=35

comment:
Thanks for the clear test page.

**Analysis**

The cause is a contract mismatch in `H264::WriteExtraData` in [H264.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H264.cpp#1493). The function writes its own NAL header byte before the SPS and the PPS, and it adds 1 to each length. The encoder callers give it complete NAL units that already start with the header byte. Thus the SPS starts with `67 67`, the PPS starts with `68 68`, and each entry is one byte too long.

The shared caller is `AnnexB::ExtractExtraDataForAVCC` in [AnnexB.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/AnnexB.cpp#458). The Windows encoder ([WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp#136)), the FFmpeg encoders ([FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#963)) and the Android encoder ([AndroidDataEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/android/AndroidDataEncoder.cpp#390)) use it. The libx264 path calls `WriteExtraData` directly ([FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#1035)). The code shows the same problem on Android, but nobody confirmed it on a device yet. macOS uses a separate writer in `AppleVTEncoder`, so it does not show the problem.

As comment 5 says, the mismatch dates from bug 1570337. It is not a recent regression.

**Next steps**

The patch in comment 5 (D334650) follows the fix direction: copy complete NAL units as they are, and add the header only in `CreateExtraData`. The current gtest `H264.AnnexBExtractExtraDataForAVCC` does not compare the SPS and PPS bytes, so a byte-exact check can prevent this problem again.

Bug 2049470 and bug 2031056 report the same defect. Because the patch is on this bug, we suggest that a person closes them as duplicates of this bug. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

comment:
Thank you for the report and the test page.

**Analysis**

Firefox gives the correct timestamp to the Windows Media Foundation encoder (MFT). But it then copies the MFT output sample time into the chunk without a check. [WMFMediaDataEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFMediaDataEncoder.cpp#518) reads the output time with `GetSampleTime()`. Line 545 writes it to the encoded frame. [VideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoEncoder.cpp#590) then uses that value as `EncodedVideoChunk.timestamp`. So the shift of one frame duration (0 + 500 = 500, 500 + 250 = 750) comes from the MFT, and Firefox trusts it.

The test page uses `avc1.64001f` (High profile) with the default latency mode and hardware preference. For non-realtime use, [MFTEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFTEncoder.cpp#805) turns off low latency mode, and Firefox does not set the B-frame count. This can let the MFT reorder frames or change the output times. The WPT `full-cycle-test` checks timestamps only with Baseline profile and `prefer-software`, so CI does not see this.

**Fix direction**

1. Keep the time and duration of each input frame in `WMFMediaDataEncoder`.
2. Give each output chunk the time of its matching input frame, not the MFT time.
3. Set the B-frame count to 0 where the MFT allows it, because WebCodecs has no decode timestamp.
4. Add a WPT case with High profile, hardware allowed and different frame durations.

This bug now blocks bug 1746557, the WebCodecs meta bug.
title: AVC VideoEncoder shifts EncodedVideoChunk timestamps by their duration

After bug 1886378, [generate_sources_mozbuild.sh](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/media/libvpx/generate_sources_mozbuild.sh#256) gives the same option to `gen_config_files` and `gen_rtcd_header`, as `disable_sve` shows. For a build with an old toolchain, note comment 5: `rtcd.pl` needs `--disable-neon_i8mm` with an underscore, but configure takes `--disable-neon-i8mm`.
